clue.text: Girl rejected by emperor in India

definitions.note: a locational definition: a place in India

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the girl's name is written from its end to its start

parts.note: the title of the Russian emperor

explanation.surface: A young woman is turned down by an emperor while in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In India' is a thin definition: it only points to some place in that country, and the wordplay pins it down.
explanation.definitionFit: Amritsar is a city in the Punjab, home of the Golden Temple of the Sikhs.

clue.text: Peter's trained as a film star

indicators.note: something trained has been shaped and reworked, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: the name with its possessive, letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Peter has trained to become a movie actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl Streep is an American actress, one of the most celebrated performers in cinema.

clue.text: Hemp derivative, as is used for stress

indicators.note: a derivative is made out of something else, so these letters are reworked into a new word

explanation.surface: Something made from hemp is used to relieve stress, a sly nod to cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' sounds like anxiety in the surface; it is the weight laid on a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress and emphasis both mean the extra force or importance placed on a syllable or idea.

clue.text: Kind of cedar used to construct dreadnought

indicators.note: to construct is to build, so the letters supplied are assembled into a new shape

parts.note: the warship split in two: dread kept whole, nought becoming the round letter for zero

explanation.surface: Cedar wood is used to build a battleship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadnought' splits into dread and nought; the second part becomes a single letter before all six letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The deodar is a Himalayan cedar tree, valued for its durable timber.

clue.text: Nothing in the meter? Far from it

indicators.note: the round letter for nothing sits inside the measuring device's letters
the answer is far from the original word, so its letters move away from their first order

parts.note: taken as written, in the American spelling
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Is the meter reading zero? Not at all, comes the reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far from it' looks like a reply meaning 'not at all'; 'Far' is the definition and the rest says the letters end up far from their order.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote means distant or a long way off, the same sense as far.

clue.text: You could be better prepared without one

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for one is taken out

explanation.surface: A self-help line: you might be better prepared if you did without something.
explanation.walkthrough: READIER loses its I to leave READER. 'You' is the definition: whoever is reading the clue is a reader.
explanation.definitionFit: The person addressed by the printed words is the one reading them, so the definition fits whoever solves it.

clue.text: Take a bearing south — from Dunkirk, no doubt?

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer: the place reached by heading south from Dunkirk

parts.note: bearing as in manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: Navigating by compass, you head south from the French Channel port of Dunkirk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like a compass reading; here it means carriage or demeanour.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a city in northern France lying due south of the port of Dunkirk.

clue.text: Pretend to be an Asian healer

explanation.surface: Someone poses as a traditional Asian doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal priest and healer, originally among the peoples of Siberia and Central Asia.

clue.text: Company of superior snobs?

parts.note: surface reading: a gathering of the most snooty people
setter's reading: snob is an old word for a cobbler, so this is a livery company of high-class shoemakers

explanation.walkthrough: Snob once meant a shoemaker or cobbler; the London livery company of fine leather shoemakers bears the answer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Worshipful Company of Cordwainers is the City of London guild of makers of fine leather shoes.

clue.text: Spite found in many a girl

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so a great many

explanation.surface: Spitefulness is to be seen in plenty of girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' looks like a container signal, but the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to harm others, the same ill will as spite.

clue.text: For operation under cover one needs an insidious type

explanation.surface: A covert operation calls for a sly, deceitful operative.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'insidious type' is a snake, the archetype of treachery since Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophidian means a snake or snake-like creature, and the serpent is proverbially sly and treacherous.

clue.text: Where to obtain some pottage

definitions.note: a place to obtain a meal, read with what follows
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the dining hall where servicemen get their food
second meaning: a portion of soft food, as in Esau's biblical dish of pottage

explanation.surface: Directions to a place selling thick soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Esau sold his birthright for a proverbial dish of pottage, and that dish's old name is also the place soldiers and sailors eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a serving of soft food and the room where military personnel take their meals.

clue.text: What train speed may turn out to be

definitions.text: What train speed may turn out to be

indicators.note: to turn out is to be rearranged into a new form, so these letters change places

explanation.surface: A grumble that trains are often disappointingly slow.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a slow train runs at a walking, dull pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian means dull and plodding, at walking pace, which describes a disappointing train service.

clue.text: Asiatic horse walks off with prizes

definitions.note: singular in the clue, the answer is a plural

indicators.note: off means wrong or disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wild horse from Asia walks away carrying trophies.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives a singular horse, while the answer is the plural, a small flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Przewalski's horse is a rare wild horse of the Mongolian steppes, named after a Russian explorer.

clue.text: Gay demon, unlikely to have sex with his own kind

definitions.note: loosely, mating within one's own group

indicators.note: an unlikely version is an improbable rearrangement, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A joke about a gay demon and his chances of mating with his own species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Own kind' looks like a same-sex joke; it means the same tribe or social group.
explanation.definitionFit: Endogamy is the custom of marrying only within one's own tribe, caste or social group.

clue.text: Actors have to be getting unfair treatment

parts.note: actors are required to be members, that is in the union
Equity is the British actors' trade union

explanation.surface: Performers forced to put up with being badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the actors' union in Britain; actors traditionally had to be in it to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequity means injustice or unfairness, the quality of treatment that is not even-handed.

clue.text: Fliers set out afresh to attack

indicators.note: laid out afresh means arranged anew, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Airmen take off once more on a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afresh' might be read as fodder, but the airmen and the word set supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Something to go on the drinks bill?

definitions.text: Something to go on the drinks bill?

parts.note: the bar's, belonging to the place serving drinks

explanation.surface: An item to be added to the tab at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as the bar's a/c: a bottle of this would indeed be charged to the drinks account.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white Bordeaux wine, the kind of thing that ends up on a bar tab.

clue.text: Guests at Blair's ball?

parts.note: Tony Blair, as Prime Minister, lived at Number 10 Downing Street
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Who came to the party thrown by the Prime Minister?
explanation.walkthrough: The British Prime Minister lives at Number Ten Downing Street, so Blair's is TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendance is the number of people present, the guests collectively.

clue.text: Priest has turned prophet

parts.note: Eli, the priest who raised Samuel

indicators.note: turned means changed around, so these three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A priest has become a prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the crossword's favourite priest, from the First Book of Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Elisha was the Old Testament prophet who succeeded Elijah.

clue.text: Before soldiers performed once again

indicators.note: the soldiers perform inside, so their letters are placed within the word for before

explanation.surface: Soldiers do their act for a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Encore is French for again, shouted to ask performers to repeat a piece.

clue.text: Afternoon test

wordplay.note: after noon it is no longer a.m., that is ex-a.m.

explanation.walkthrough: Once noon passes the morning is over: EX (former) + AM (morning).
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is an examination, a formal written or oral assessment of knowledge.

clue.text: To skive is bad in France and in parts of Germany

parts.note: standard abbreviation, a part of the name

explanation.surface: Shirking work is frowned on in France and in some regions of Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skive' is British slang for dodging work or school.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to fake illness to avoid work, which is the British idea of skiving.

clue.text: One taken aboard vessel for voyage

indicators.note: something taken aboard is carried inside, so the letter goes into the vessel

parts.note: a cruse is a small earthenware jar for oil or water

explanation.surface: A passenger joins a ship for a sea journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship but is a cruse, a small jar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise is a pleasure trip by sea, a kind of voyage.

clue.text: Dig up old philosopher

explanation.surface: Excavate the remains of a long-dead thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to unearth something buried, especially a corpse.

clue.text: Where it's cold riding in HGV

definitions.text: Where it's cold riding in HGV

indicators.note: a passenger riding in a lorry is inside it, so the letter sits within

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a heavy goods vehicle
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A chilly ride in the cab of a heavy goods lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: HGV is the British term for a heavy goods vehicle; an artic is an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic is the polar region around the North Pole, famously the coldest of places.
